about.title: About me
about.text: I'm a software engineer with a passion for building efficient, scalable, and user-friendly applications. My journey started with a fascination for how things work behind the screen, and quickly evolved into a career focused on creating impactful digital solutions. Over the past few years, I've worked on diverse projects—ranging from productivity tools to enterprise healthcare systems, IoT platforms, and industrial automation. I thrive on solving complex problems and delivering solutions that make a real difference.

meta.title: AI & Intelligent Automation - Kajoble
meta.description: Specialist in AI-driven automation and intelligent workflow design. Engineering-first approach for production-ready AI systems.

banner.title: AI, Automation & Intelligent Workflows
banner.subtitle: Transforming AI from experimentation to production-ready systems. Engineering-first approach to intelligent automation.

intro.title: AI-Driven Automation & Intelligent Workflows
intro.p1: I specialize in artificial intelligence-driven automation and the design of intelligent workflows that connect software systems, data, and decision-making processes.
intro.p2: My work focuses on building practical, production-ready solutions using tools such as n8n to automate complex workflows, orchestrate APIs, and integrate AI capabilities into existing systems. I make extensive, professional use of modern AI assistants and developer tools — including ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Google AI Studio, and Google Labs — to accelerate development, improve code quality, and support advanced problem-solving.

philosophy.title: Engineering-First Philosophy
philosophy.p1: My approach to AI is engineering-first: I focus on robustness, automation, and real business value rather than experimentation alone. The goal is always the same — turn AI into a dependable system component, not just a standalone feature.
philosophy.p2: This means prioritizing production readiness, maintainability, observability, and integration with existing systems. AI solutions should be reliable infrastructure, not fragile prototypes.
